title: Service pages (all 7): choose the structure
question: One shared template for every service page (CRM, automations, websites, landing pages, apps, e-commerce, UI/UX). Pick the composition, or re-roll.

options.label: Service Landing, Pad-Built
options.lineage: the familiar service page, executed in the pad world
options.thesis: Hero with the service promise and action, then what's included, how it works, real work, questions, and a closing slip.
options.viewport: Carbon field: service name as Karantina headline, tagline, tear-slip CTA with reply stamp, WhatsApp line. Below: long description as a readable column, features as ruled lines, process steps with durations, client copies, FAQ, related services, closing slip.
options.risk: Familiar order; distinction lives in the pad parts.

options.label: The Work Order
options.lineage: a printed work-order form for this job
options.thesis: The page is the order form for this service: what's included is ticked, the schedule is printed, the fine print answers questions.
options.viewport: A tall paper sheet on carbon: form header with service name and No., ticked included-items list, a schedule table (step, what happens, duration), then fine-print FAQ and a tear-off slip at the bottom edge to order.
options.risk: Form metaphor can make long SEO text feel cramped; needs generous reading width.

regions.label: form header: service name, No., CTA

options.label: Answers First
options.lineage: the questions owners actually ask before buying
options.thesis: Lead with the price, time and fit questions people search for; features and work back up the answers.
options.viewport: Short carbon hero with the service name and CTA, then the FAQ as the main column (price, time, how it differs) with a sticky order slip beside it; features, process and work follow as supporting evidence.
options.risk: Pushes the offer narrative below dense answers; weaker for visitors who are not comparison shopping.
